youtube.comment: You asked for it – science! @Jo-wl5fj, how many did you get? Everyone else: comment your score out of 30 👇

lines.q: Thirty science questions, five seconds each, get twenty and you pass! First one: what is the chemical formula for water?
lines.a: H two O! Two hydrogens, one oxygen.

lines.q: How many legs does an insect have?
lines.a: Six! Spiders have eight, so they're not insects.

lines.q: Which organ pumps blood around your body?
lines.a: The heart! It never takes a day off.

lines.q: What do caterpillars turn into?
lines.a: Butterflies! Or moths.

lines.q: Which gas do we need to breathe in?
lines.a: Oxygen! We breathe out carbon dioxide.

lines.q: Plants make food from sunlight by what process?
lines.a: Photosynthesis! Easy round done. Now it gets harder.

lines.q: Medium round! What is the chemical symbol for sodium?
lines.a: N A! From its old Latin name, natrium.

lines.q: Animals that eat only plants are called what?
lines.a: Herbivores! Like cows and rabbits.

lines.q: The energy of a moving object is called what?
lines.a: Kinetic! From the Greek word for motion.

lines.q: What is called the powerhouse of the cell?
lines.a: Mitochondria! They turn food into energy. If you're enjoying this, subscribe and turn on the bell!

lines.q: What is the pH of pure water?
lines.a: Seven! Right in the middle, neutral.

lines.q: Which gas makes party balloons float?
lines.a: Helium! Lighter than air, and it won't burn.

lines.q: Hard round! What is the chemical symbol for tin?
lines.a: S N! From the Latin stannum.

lines.q: Who made the first vaccine, back in seventeen ninety six?
lines.a: Edward Jenner! Against smallpox.

lines.q: Electrical resistance is measured in what?
lines.a: Ohms! Named after Georg Ohm.

lines.q: How many chromosomes do humans usually have?
lines.a: Forty six! Twenty three pairs.

lines.q: Who discovered penicillin in nineteen twenty eight?
lines.a: Alexander Fleming! Thanks to a mouldy dish.

lines.q: Which acid is in your stomach?
lines.a: Hydrochloric! A special lining keeps it from eating your stomach.

lines.q: Very hard round! Absolute zero is about how many degrees Celsius?
lines.a: Minus two hundred seventy three! Nothing gets colder.

lines.q: Which element has the symbol S B?
lines.a: Antimony! From the Latin stibium.

lines.q: What is the S I unit of force?
lines.a: The newton! Named after Isaac Newton.

lines.q: What is the most common protein in your body?
lines.a: Collagen! It holds skin and bones together.

lines.q: Who put the Sun at the centre of the universe, in fifteen forty three?
lines.a: Copernicus! In the year he died.

lines.q: Which vitamin helps your blood clot?
lines.a: Vitamin K! Leafy greens are full of it. Still with me? Legend round next!

lines.q: Legend round! How many elements are on the periodic table?
lines.a: One hundred eighteen! The last four were named in twenty sixteen.

lines.q: Who measured the electron's charge with oil drops?
lines.a: Robert Millikan! Nobel Prize in nineteen twenty three.

lines.q: Which mineral is number one on the Mohs hardness scale?
lines.a: Talc! Soft enough to scratch with a fingernail. Three left, stay with me!

lines.q: Which element is named after Poland?
lines.a: Polonium! Marie Curie named it after her homeland.

lines.q: Which element is the most electronegative?
lines.a: Fluorine! It grabs electrons like nothing else.

lines.q: Last one. Carbon fourteen's half life is about how long?
lines.a: Five thousand seven hundred thirty years! That's how we date old bones.
